question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}+\sqrt{y-4}} & = \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{y}+\sqrt{y-4}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}}{\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}}{(\sqrt{y}+\sqrt{y-4})(\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4})} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}}{(\sqrt{y})^{2}-(\sqrt{y-4})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}}{y-(y-4)} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{y}-\sqrt{y-4}}{4} & \end{aligned}
$$
